title: Australian politics live: Plibersek warns One Nation support ‘winding back access’ to abortion; NSW to waive stamp duty for restructuring trusts
text: 20.35 EDT Unemployment holds at 4.7% in September Patrick Commins Unemployment held at 4.7% in September, after the economy shed 39,300 jobs in the month and amid fears the Reserve Bank could hike interest rates for a fifth time when it next meets. The Australian Bureau of Statistics figures would have shown the jobless rate ticking higher last month had it not revised up the August figure from 4.6% to 4.7%. Full-time employment increased by 34,400 in September, but this was more than offset by a sharp drop in part-time employment of 73,700. Underemployment, which includes those with jobs but trying to find more work, lifted to 6.3%, from 6.2% in September. Economists had identified this week’s labour force statistics as a key bit of information for the RBA ahead of its next interest rate decision on 3 November. Financial markets this morning, and before the latest data, put a 40% chance of a hike on Melbourne Cup day, which would be the fifth for the year as the central bank attempts to bring inflation back towards its 2.5% target over the coming 12 months.
author: Krishani Dhanji

title: Labor and Coalition set to reject bill to stop incarcerated women being shackled in childbirth
text: Labor and the Coalition have rejected a bill that would have banned the shackling of incarcerated women during childbirth, Photograph: Penny Stephens/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Labor and the Coalition have rejected a bill that would have banned the shackling of incarcerated women during childbirth, Photograph: Penny Stephens/The Guardian Birth rights Australian politics Labor and Coalition block bill that would ban incarcerated women being shackled in childbirth Liberal Paul Scarr breaks ranks to condemn major parties, saying he will write to Queensland attorney general Krishani Dhanji and Tory Shepherd Wed 14 Oct 2026 20.22 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 20.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Labor and the Coalition have blocked a vote on a bill that would have banned the shackling of incarcerated women during childbirth, with the government saying it was the responsibility of the states and territories. title: Trump tries to rally support for Republican candidates as top Super Pac for Senate Democrats pours millions into key races – live
text: 14.41 EDT Top Senate Democratic Super Pac pours millions more in Michigan and Maine races The top Super Pac for Senate Democrats will pour more than $7m into two marquee races this cycle: Michigan and Maine. The Senate Majority Pac has reserved $3.7m for its campaign in Michigan, to support the Democratic nominee , Dr Abdul El-Sayed , against the Trump-backed Republican, Mike Rogers . The group is also investing $3m in Maine , to boost Democrat Troy Jackson’s chances against Susan Collins – the five-term moderate GOP incumbent, who Democrats see as increasingly vulnerable in a cycle where anti-Trump sentiment has colored much of the election. This comes after reports that the Senate Majority Pac has also paused ad spending in North Carolina and Georgia. Semafor was first to report on the updated spend.
author: Cecilia Nowell (now); Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
